_comment: EA conformance cases where custos intentionally differs (see the rule spec's Divergences section). Keys: '<test>#<method>/<fixture basename>' as printed by TestEA; values: reason.
src/test/java/com/kalessil/phpStorm/phpI: fix emits PHPUnit's real method names (assertFileDoesNotExist / assertDirectoryDoesNotExist) instead of upstream's misspelled ones
upstream's IDE formatter re-spaces an unreported `array& $arr` parameter; custos edits only the reported ranges

upstream's IDE formatter re-spaces an untouched inner for header (custos copies the body verbatim); additionally a limit variable reused by several loops is resolved from the assignment reaching each loop (one extra report); loops whose counter or header-assigned limit is mentioned after the loop are not reported (two fewer reports)
below PHP 8.0 no fix when the array may have string keys (unpacking would throw)
loose ==/!= forms are not reported: they ignore key order and are not equivalent to array_is_list()
array-typed arguments are spread via ...array_values() so string keys neither throw (<8.1) nor collide (>=8.1)
get_parent_class() in a class without extends is not rewritten to parent::class (fatal error)
get_class() outside a class is not rewritten to __CLASS__ (empty there); version_compare(..., '7.1', '==') not rewritten (patch level makes it non-equivalent)
reported without a fix: get_debug_type() names differ from gettype() for scalars (int/integer, float/double, null/NULL)

only exact equivalents get a fix (is_a, get_class on a final class, class_implements with an interface literal on an object); get_parent_class/is_subclass_of/class_parents and non-final get_class are reported without a fix
the or-form re-check emits || is_dir($concurrentDirectory) (upstream negates it, inverting the logic)
below PHPUnit 9.1 the fix suggests assertFileNotExists/assertDirectoryNotExists (the DoesNotExist names do not exist yet)
no fix below PHP 7.0 (?? does not parse); ?? '' guard from 7.0; negative offsets other than -1 skipped (strlen($s) - n can go negative)
4-argument mb_substr fix emits mb_strpos($h, $n, 0, $enc); case-folded comparisons only against literals already in folded case
calls with call-time & arguments are not reported/rewritten ($fn($a, &$b) is a fatal error since PHP 5.4)
an override that calls the parent without return, where the parent returns a value, is not reported (removing it would change return values)
the generated limit variable avoids names already used in the scope ($iMax1 instead of overwriting $iMax)
assertInternalType is reported only when the declared return type always satisfies the named type; unknown/contradicting type names are not reported (that call fails, it is not redundant)
method/static calls are not reordered (they may have side effects); isset($x[...]) && $x is not reported (isset also guards $x itself)
under && the broader (redundant) instanceof is reported, not the more specific one
an own property incompatible with the trait's (different default, visibility, static, readonly or type) is reported as an error: PHP refuses to compose such a class
keys are compared as PHP stores them (escapes decoded, '7' == 7, any integer base); duplicate integer keys are reported too
for a bool operand the fix emits x() instead of false !== x()
no suggestion when the declaration would be a compile error (": void" with return $x where $x is null/void-documented, "?T" with a bare return)
a private untyped property without default (and not assigned by the constructor) holds null until written, so a cast of it is not redundant even when its @var names the target type
